title: Control ownership handoff - 1:1 prep (SOC2/ISO)
content:
Meeting: 1:1 w/ Marco Ruiz (control owner handoff)
Date: 2026-03-11 10:30am PT (prep notes)
Goal: walk Marco through control bundle for CCM, confirm evidence sources, agree on recurring evidence tasks and handoff dates; surface any control gaps before readiness dry-run.

Top objectives (short):
- Confirm owners for SOC2 CC1/CC3/CC6 controls we maintain (specifically: access reviews, change mgmt, vendor due diligence).
- Validate where evidence lives (S3 buckets, Datadog dashboards, Confluence runbooks).
- Capture quick wins to reduce audit friction (templated evidence exports, checklist for reviewers).
- Decide on escalation path for third-party control failures (who pings legal / procurement).

Agenda (10–15m each section):
1) Quick status (2m): my read of readiness score + most urgent gaps.
2) Ownership walk (8m): map each control -> owner -> current evidence.
   - CC6 (change mgmt): currently assigned to Marco? TODO: confirm. Evidence: git tags + release notes in GH-releases (repo: infra/deploys).
   - CC7 (access provisioning): Leah is backup; we need monthly attestation exports from Okta (okta-report-2026-02).
   - CC3 (system monitoring): SRE owns alerts but evidence dashboards vary (datadog:infra/high-cpu, app/errors).
3) Evidence gaps (6m): list missing or manual pieces.
4) Action items & deadlines (4m): assign owner + target date.
5) Parking lot / questions to raise with audit team (1m).

Notes to self (raw):
- Prep quick reference: one-pager showing evidence path for 8 critical controls. Make PDF and pin to the confluence page linked above.
- Keep language audit-friendly: "monthly attestation" not "we check sometimes".
- Ask Marco if his team can do weekly snapshot exports (S3) instead of on-demand pulls. That reduces manual QA time.

Control mapping (quick text table):
- CC3: System Monitoring -> Owner: SRE (Sam). Evidence: Datadog dashboard (link), incident runbook ids, pagerduty incidents.
- CC6: Change Management -> Owner: Marco Ruiz (candidate). Evidence: GH release tags, PR review logs, deploy approval tickets (JIRA: DEPLOY-*).
- CC7: Access Provisioning/Revocation -> Owner: Leah Patel (backup). Evidence: Okta reports, GSuite admin audit, IAM policy docs.
- Vendor Risk: procurement + vendor-risk -> Owner: Procurement (TBD). Evidence: signed contracts, vendor questionnaires in 3rd-party vault.

Open questions to resolve in meeting:
- Marco: can you point me to the canonical location where release artifacts are stored today? (S3 path, repo name)
- Marco/Leah: do you have a standard retention policy for evidence snapshots? If not, propose 12 months rolling.
- Who owns mapping for subcontractors? Need clear owner for vendor components that support our infra (e.g., managed DB).

Immediate action items (post-1:1):
- Ivy: create one-pager evidence map (due 2026-03-13).
- Marco: confirm change mgmt evidence locations + give read access to audit account (due 2026-03-17).
- Leah: schedule monthly Okta export job + share sample CSV (due 2026-03-16).
- Procurement: drop vendor questionnaire answers into shared vault and ping security (linked_artifact JIRA-SEC-322) (due 2026-03-20).
- SRE (Sam): confirm Datadog dashboard export process and snapshot cadence (due 2026-03-18).

Evidence checklist (for quick handoff):
- Automated export? Y/N
- File path / dashboard URL (explicit)
- Owner + backup + contact email
- Retention policy
- Notes about manual steps (if any)

Audit prep script (short):
- If auditor asks for monthly access attestation: pull Okta report -> save as CSV -> upload to S3/path -> notify audit@g.redwood.ai with link.
- If auditor requests change history: point to GH release log + JIRA deploy tickets with approvals. Zip and provide link.

Draft phrasing for 1:1 to keep conversation efficient:
"Marco — the objective for this sync is to make sure we can hand off CC6 evidence in a way the auditor can reproduce. Walk me through where deploy artifacts live and who approves. If we can set up automated snapshots for releases and Okta exports, we should be able to move most evidence work to routine ops instead of ad-hoc requests"

Parking lot / escalate to legal / procurement if:
- Vendor refuses to provide SOC2-type evidence or refuses to sign addendum.
- Evidence retention insufficient for 12 months and vendor can't change.

Reference links (quick):
- Confluence control matrix: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SOC2/Control+Matrix
- Example Okta export location: s3://redwood-evidence/okta/monthly/okta-2026-02.csv
- JIRA ticket to raise if vendor issues: JIRA-SEC-322

Post-meeting follow-up template (to send within 24h):
Subject: Notes + actions from SOC2 control-ownership 1:1 (Marco)
Body: short bullets: confirmed owners, attachments (one-pager), action items + deadlines, link to confluence, cc: Leah, Sam, procurement.

Quick hacks if running out of time in meeting:
- If no time to map all controls, prioritize: CC6 (change mgmt), CC7 (access), CC3 (monitoring).
- Ask for 1 concrete artifact now (e.g., last month Okta CSV) so auditor can test sample.

End of scratchpad.
notes_short: prep scratchpad for convo with Marco re: control evidence, owners, quick wins
